description: Load-following MSR with Xe-135/I-135 dynamics. MSR unique: online fuel reprocessing removes Xe continuously, reducing xenon deadtime. Reactivity feedback from fuel salt temperature coefficient is strongly negative.

unit.name: Generic 1 GWth / 400 MWe Fluoride MSR (MSBR-class)
unit.source: Haubenreich & Engel (1970) ORNL-4394; MacPherson (1985) Nucl. Sci. Eng. 90:374-380; Delpech et al. (2009) J. Fluorine Chem. 130:11-17; NEA (2021) Molten Salt Reactor Handbook.

P_thermal_mw.note: Thermal power at full load (MSBR reference 1000 MWth)

eta_thermal.note: Net thermal efficiency (MSR operates at ~700C, supercritical CO2 or high-pressure steam cycle -> ~40%)

sigma_Xe_cm2.note: Xe-135 microscopic absorption cross-section (same fission product)

ramp_rate_limit_pct_min.note: MSR has faster load-following than PWR: liquid fuel, no structural thermal stress, online reprocessing frees Xe constraint; ~10%/min feasible

PLR_min.note: MSR can load-follow deeply (20-100%), liquid fuel avoids xenon preclude problem

total_reactivity_margin_pcm.note: Lower margin needed because xenon is continuously stripped by off-gas system

xenon_reactivity_coeff_pcm.note: Effective Xe penalty is reduced vs solid-fuel reactors because online reprocessing strips Xe from liquid salt (typical 50% reduction)

xe_strip_efficiency.note: Fraction of Xe continuously removed by off-gas system per decay constant time; 0.5 = 50% effective removal rate

fuel_temp_coeff_pcm_per_K.note: Fuel salt temperature reactivity coefficient; large negative value (liquid fuel Doppler + expansion) provides inherent safety

T_fuel_rated_C.note: Fuel salt temperature at rated power (average of hot/cold leg)
